newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt rises on Brazil Brady swap/buyback offer.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt rises on Brazil Brady swap/buyback offer.

text.p: Brazil rocked the emerging debt market Wednesday morning when it unveiled its offer to swap or buy back Brady bonds, and that news set off a sustained surge in prices, traders said.
The most powerful gains were in Brazilian paper, but the movement lead to mild gains across the market, at the same time as the U.S. Treasury market slumped.
"Brazil in general is going to perform well in the short term given this buyback," said the chief Brady trader at a U.S. investment bank. "It had a big impact on other countries."

Brazil offered to either repurchase outright Par bonds BR4D24=RR, and Discount Z-L bonds BRFLTD24=RR or to swap Pars, Discounts, or "C" bonds BR8D14=RR Bradies for up to $1.0 billion of 30-year uncollaterized global bonds.
The offer will expire at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT on June 3, unless extended or ended earlier by Brazil.
By the end of trade, price talk for the global bonds was around 350 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan will act as joint managers of the deal
Several investors declined comment on the merits of the deal, citing the need to review the implications of the deal.
One investor cited reports that most of the trade Wednesday was driven by proprietary trading houses, with only one insurance company in on the action.
By the close, the more liquid "C" bond rose 1-3/8 to 78-5/8 bid, while Discounts were up 1-3/8 to 82-1/2, and Pars were up one point to 65-7/8.
It was a stirring day, as Brazilian paper tightened 25-40 basis points, despite negative pressure from U.S. Treasuries. The benchmark U.S. 30-year bond closed 23/32 lower to 6.96 percent.
"What stopped things in its tracks was pressure on the long end in the U.S. Treasury market," one trader said. "Without that we would have been 50-75 bps tighter in Brazil."
Some Brady traders projected that Brazil had a good chance to sustain its gains, given that Brasilia seemed to be taking a more active liability management.
"This will be enough reason for the market to speculate on the upside," one dealer said.
